punctuated: 天地無以肇其體，天地非禮樂無以顯其用。是故天地奠位於上下，萬物散殊於其間，乃質具異序而不可以強同，禮之制則行於此矣。周流有不息之機，合同有化醇之妙，乃氣行同和而不容以獨異，樂之情則興於此焉。何則？春而作，夏而長，一陽氣之周流而為生物之仁；秋而斂，冬而藏，一陰氣之凝寂而為成物之義。仁雖不足以言樂，而春夏生物之仁即周流同化之機，仁豈不近於樂乎？義雖不足以言禮，而秋冬成物之義即高下散殊之妙，義豈不近於禮乎？夫禮樂之肇乎造化如此，而其用之合乎造化何如？彼其備五聲六律、以和為主者，聖人之樂也。是樂也，使作之長之，有以厚其氣之同；厚同則循其春夏陽氣之伸，而與天同妙生物之仁也，非率神而從天者乎？具節文度數、以序為主者，聖人之禮也。是禮也，使斂之藏之，有以辨其物之異；辨異則斂其秋冬陰氣之屈，而與地同妙成物之義也，非居鬼而從地者乎？吁！禮樂肇於
translation_en:
…without Heaven and Earth, could not originate in their essential forms; without rites and music, Heaven and Earth could not manifest their operation. Thus Heaven and Earth establish their positions above and below, and the myriad things are distributed in their diversity between them. Their material forms possess distinct orders and cannot be forced into uniformity: here the institutions of ritual operate. In ceaseless circulation lies the impulse that never rests; in union lies the marvel of transformation into a harmonious whole. Vital energies thus move in shared harmony and cannot remain separately distinct: here the inner spirit of music arises. Why is this so? Spring brings forth and summer nurtures growth: this is entirely the circulation of yang energy, constituting the benevolence that gives life to things. Autumn gathers in and winter stores away: this is entirely the still concentration of yin energy, constituting the righteousness that brings things to completion. Although benevolence alone does not suffice to describe music, the benevolence that gives life to things in spring and summer is precisely the impulse of circulation and shared transformation. Is benevolence not close to music? Although righteousness alone does not suffice to describe ritual, the righteousness that brings things to completion in autumn and winter is precisely the marvel of differentiation into high and low and distribution in diversity. Is righteousness not close to ritual?
If this is how rites and music originate in the creative transformations of nature, how does their operation accord with those transformations? That which comprises the five notes and six pitch standards and takes harmony as its guiding principle is the music of the sages. Such music brings things forth and nurtures their growth, thereby deepening the unity of their vital energies. By deepening this unity, it follows the expansion of yang energy in spring and summer and shares with Heaven the wondrous working of the benevolence that gives life to things. Does it not thereby lead the spirits and follow Heaven? That which comprises ceremonial forms, measures, and prescribed numbers and takes order as its guiding principle is the ritual of the sages. Such ritual gathers things in and stores them away, thereby distinguishing their differences. By distinguishing these differences, it gathers inward with the contraction of yin energy in autumn and winter and shares with Earth the wondrous working of the righteousness that brings things to completion. Does it not thereby settle the ghosts and follow Earth? Ah! Rites and music originate in…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
造化而又合乎造化如此其所以相爲流通者
歟抑觀之天地者無形之禮樂禮樂者有形之
天地也然非聖人昭揭以示人則禮樂自禮樂
天地自天地孰知天地禮樂之無二哉聖人知
此故始也法陰陽以爲禮樂終也以禮樂而賛
陰陽則天之生地之成皆得其職矣故下文曰
禮樂明備天地官矣信夫
第貳場
論
===
聖人有功於天下萬世
林士元
同考試官學正侯批題只數字意則無窮
此作能以一泓之水廣涵萬頃之波瀾一束之
毫具掃千軍之氣勢妙天人之理渙風水之文
真傑作也
考試官學正周批老健
考試官敎授張批一氣而成圓轉無疊
語讀之令人快焉真論作也
punctuated:
造化而又合乎造化，如此其所以相爲流通者歟？抑觀之，天地者，無形之禮樂；禮樂者，有形之天地也。然非聖人昭揭以示人，則禮樂自禮樂，天地自天地，孰知天地禮樂之無二哉？聖人知此，故始也法陰陽以爲禮樂，終也以禮樂而賛陰陽，則天之生、地之成皆得其職矣。故下文曰：「禮樂明備，天地官矣。」信夫！

第貳場
論

聖人有功於天下萬世
林士元

同考試官學正侯批：「題只數字，意則無窮。此作能以一泓之水，廣涵萬頃之波瀾；一束之毫，具掃千軍之氣勢。妙天人之理，渙風水之文，真傑作也。」

考試官學正周批：「老健。」

考試官敎授張批：「一氣而成，圓轉無疊語，讀之令人快焉，真論作也。」
translation_en:
…the processes of creation and transformation, and yet also accord with them: is this how they flow into and through one another? Consider further: Heaven and Earth are ritual and music without visible form; ritual and music are Heaven and Earth in visible form. Yet unless the sage clearly revealed this to humankind, ritual and music would remain merely ritual and music, and Heaven and Earth merely Heaven and Earth. Who would know that Heaven and Earth and ritual and music are not two separate things? The sage understood this. Thus, at the outset he modeled ritual and music on yin and yang; ultimately, through ritual and music he assisted yin and yang. Heaven’s generation and Earth’s completion of things thereby each fulfill their proper function. Hence the passage below says: “When ritual and music are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth perform their offices.” How true!

Second Session
Discourse

“The Sages Have Rendered Service to All under Heaven for Myriad Generations”
By Lin Shiyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Hou, School Instructor: “The topic consists of only a few characters, yet its meaning is inexhaustible. This composition can encompass the waves of ten thousand expanses of water within a single pool, and wield, with a single brush, the force to sweep away a thousand armies. It treats the principles of Heaven and humankind with subtle mastery; its prose spreads like wind over water. A true masterpiece!”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: “Seasoned and vigorous.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “Completed in a single sustained breath, it turns smoothly, without repetitive phrasing. Reading it gives delight. This is truly a discourse!”

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
論曰聖人以一身之動而垂澤於無窮必
其道有不可易者矣夫動必本諸道而後
事可成功可立大可以及於天下遠可以
及於萬世苟無道以主之則是私意小知
之為而吾之所以自立者先無其本矣况
望其利天下澤後世也哉甚矣道之不可
易也天地之所以為天地人物之所以為
人物不能外此道也道之在天下其可一
日無耶彼數聖人者當草昧之初乃能以
===
天地萬物為己任其推明制作有以宜天
下之心經綸措置有以利萬世之用萬世
而下天地賴之而位萬物賴之而育不能
以有外者謂非其道之不可易耶噫此五
帝之功所以為大且遠也褒崇之典君天
下者容可不究心乎五峯胡氏斯言其闢
異端扶正道之意有在矣愚嘗觀道之在
天地間無物不有無時不然天地之所以
高深鬼神之所以幽遠山川之所以流峙
punctuated: 論曰：聖人以一身之動而垂澤於無窮，必其道有不可易者矣。夫動必本諸道，而後事可成，功可立，大可以及於天下，遠可以及於萬世。苟無道以主之，則是私意小知之為，而吾之所以自立者先無其本矣，况望其利天下、澤後世也哉！甚矣，道之不可易也！天地之所以為天地，人物之所以為人物，不能外此道也。道之在天下，其可一日無耶？彼數聖人者，當草昧之初，乃能以天地萬物為己任。其推明制作，有以宜天下之心；經綸措置，有以利萬世之用。萬世而下，天地賴之而位，萬物賴之而育，不能以有外者，謂非其道之不可易耶？噫！此五帝之功所以為大且遠也。褒崇之典，君天下者容可不究心乎？五峯胡氏斯言，其闢異端、扶正道之意有在矣。愚嘗觀道之在天地間，無物不有，無時不然。天地之所以高深，鬼神之所以幽遠，山川之所以流峙，
translation_en: The discourse states: When a sage, through his own actions, bestows benefits without end, his Way must possess something that cannot be altered. Actions must be grounded in the Way; only then can undertakings succeed and achievements be established, extending in scope throughout all under Heaven and in duration through myriad generations. If the Way does not govern them, they are merely the workings of selfish intentions and petty understanding, and the very means by which one establishes oneself already lack their foundation. How, then, could one hope to benefit all under Heaven and bestow blessings on later ages? How utterly unalterable is the Way! That which makes Heaven and Earth Heaven and Earth, and human beings and other things what they are, cannot lie outside this Way. Could the world be without the Way for even a single day? Those several sages, living at the dawn of civilization, were nevertheless able to take Heaven, Earth, and all things as their own responsibility. Their elucidation of principles and creation of institutions answered the hearts of all under Heaven; their ordering and arrangement of affairs served the needs of myriad generations. Through all the generations since, Heaven and Earth have depended on this to occupy their proper places, and all things have depended on it to flourish, with nothing able to stand outside it. Could one deny that this was because their Way could not be altered? Ah! This is why the achievements of the Five Emperors were so great and so enduring. Could those who rule all under Heaven fail to give careful thought to the rites for honoring and exalting them? In these words of Master Hu of Wufeng, there is an intention to refute heterodox teachings and uphold the correct Way. I have reflected that, as the Way exists between Heaven and Earth, no thing is without it, and no moment is otherwise. That by which Heaven and Earth are high and deep, ghosts and spirits hidden and remote, and mountains and rivers flowing or standing firm …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
日月之所以照臨品物之所以化生與夫
一塵之微一息之頃莫非道之所寓有此
道而後有此物有此物必本於此道是道
也日用之不可違須臾之不可離事焉不
本於道則流於清淨虛無之歸雖一步不
可行一時不可立佛老之流是已惟事本
於道則道不可易而事亦不可易非惟當
世可行雖至於百千萬世之遠亦可行矣
五帝之功是已嗚呼邪正不兩立出此則
===
入彼正道明則邪說自息矣報功之典容
可以不舉乎何則太古之初聖人未出世
尚洪荒風氣未開人文未著制度未興事
功未立八索九丘未彰三墳二典未作天
地且不得為天地也而況於人乎而況於
物乎上天於此蓋有憂之而伏羲神農黃
帝堯舜數聖人相繼出焉膺上天之寄任
民牧之責將以天之意而加之民者也豈
忍恝然而弗加之意乎恝然弗加之意則
punctuated: 日月之所以照臨，品物之所以化生，與夫一塵之微、一息之頃，莫非道之所寓。有此道而後有此物，有此物必本於此道。是道也，日用之不可違，須臾之不可離。事焉不本於道，則流於清淨虛無之歸，雖一步不可行，一時不可立，佛老之流是已。惟事本於道，則道不可易，而事亦不可易。非惟當世可行，雖至於百千萬世之遠，亦可行矣，五帝之功是已。嗚呼！邪正不兩立，出此則入彼，正道明則邪說自息矣。報功之典，容可以不舉乎？何則？太古之初，聖人未出，世尚洪荒，風氣未開，人文未著，制度未興，事功未立，《八索》《九丘》未彰，《三墳》《二典》未作，天地且不得為天地也，而況於人乎？而況於物乎？上天於此蓋有憂之，而伏羲、神農、黃帝、堯、舜數聖人相繼出焉，膺上天之寄，任民牧之責，將以天之意而加之民者也。豈忍恝然而弗加之意乎？恝然弗加之意，則
translation_en:
…the means by which the sun and moon shine upon the world and the myriad things undergo transformation and come into being—even the minuteness of a speck of dust and the brief span of a breath—are all places where the Way resides. Only with this Way do these things exist; wherever these things exist, they must be rooted in this Way. This Way must not be transgressed in daily life, nor may one depart from it for even an instant. If undertakings are not rooted in the Way, they drift toward quietude, emptiness, and nothingness: one cannot advance even a single step or remain standing for even a moment. Such are the followers of the Buddha and Laozi. Only when undertakings are rooted in the Way is the Way unalterable and the undertakings likewise unalterable. They can be put into practice not only in the present age, but even hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands of generations hence. Such were the achievements of the Five Emperors.

Alas! The heterodox and the orthodox cannot stand together: leaving one, one enters the other. When the correct Way is made manifest, heterodox teachings cease of themselves. Can the rites for requiting meritorious achievement possibly be left unperformed? Why is this so? At the beginning of remote antiquity, before the sages had appeared, the world was still in a primordial wilderness. Civilizing influences had not yet unfolded, human culture had not become manifest, institutions had not arisen, and achievements had not been established. The Eight Cords (Ba suo) and Nine Hills (Jiu qiu) had not been revealed; the Three Tombs (San fen) and Two Canons (Er dian) had not been composed. Even Heaven and Earth could not yet be Heaven and Earth—how much less human beings, and how much less the other things of the world!

Heaven above was surely concerned about this, and the sages Fuxi, Shennong, Huangdi, Yao, and Shun appeared in succession. They received Heaven’s charge and assumed responsibility as shepherds of the people, intending to carry out Heaven’s purpose for the people. How could they bear to remain indifferent and give the matter no thought? If they remained indifferent and gave it no thought, then…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天之所以生我者何為我之所以受於天
者何事而民所以望我者孤矣嗚呼聖人
於此蓋有不得辭其責者矣然聖人一身
甚微也生於一時甚近也以一人而計天
下甚大也以天下而計萬世甚遠也聖人
何以有功於天下有功於萬世耶蓋必有
其道矣聖人者天之所特厚斯道之所寄
焉者也與之者厚則其望之者深蓋將以
天下民物累之也蓋將以萬世民物累之
===
也聖人者畏天命而悲人窮者也蓋有不
得辭其責矣故心代天意口代天言手代
天工身代天事不為一身計而為天下計
不為一世計而為萬世計仰觀法於天俯
觀法於地中觀萬物於人畫八卦以明陰
陽之道造書契以代結繩之政作耒耜以
成稼穡之功制衣裳以嚴上下之分民病
於居也而宮室以興民阻於險也而舟車
以制民病於夭也而醫藥以行民狃於詐
punctuated: 天之所以生我者何為？我之所以受於天者何事？而民所以望我者孤矣。嗚呼！聖人於此蓋有不得辭其責者矣。然聖人一身甚微也，生於一時甚近也；以一人而計天下，甚大也；以天下而計萬世，甚遠也。聖人何以有功於天下、有功於萬世耶？蓋必有其道矣。聖人者，天之所特厚、斯道之所寄焉者也。與之者厚，則其望之者深，蓋將以天下民物累之也，蓋將以萬世民物累之也。聖人者，畏天命而悲人窮者也，蓋有不得辭其責矣。故心代天意，口代天言，手代天工，身代天事；不為一身計，而為天下計；不為一世計，而為萬世計。仰觀法於天，俯觀法於地，中觀萬物於人，畫八卦以明陰陽之道，造書契以代結繩之政，作耒耜以成稼穡之功，制衣裳以嚴上下之分。民病於居也，而宮室以興；民阻於險也，而舟車以制；民病於夭也，而醫藥以行；民狃於詐
translation_en: …For what purpose, then, did Heaven give me life? What charge have I received from Heaven? And the people's hopes in me would be disappointed. Alas! In this the sages surely bore a responsibility they could not decline. Yet a sage, as a single individual, is very small, and his life within a single age is very brief. Measured against one individual, all under Heaven is vast; measured against the world of the present, ten thousand generations extend far into the future. How can sages render service to all under Heaven and to ten thousand generations? There must surely be a Way by which they do so. Sages are those whom Heaven has especially favored and in whom this Way is entrusted. The more richly Heaven endows them, the greater its expectations of them: it means to entrust to them the burden of the people and all things throughout the world, and of the people and all things through ten thousand generations. Sages revere Heaven's mandate and grieve at human distress; they surely cannot decline this responsibility. Thus their minds express Heaven's intentions, their mouths speak Heaven's words, their hands perform Heaven's work, and their persons carry out Heaven's affairs. They plan for all under Heaven rather than for themselves, and for ten thousand generations rather than for a single age. Looking upward, they observe patterns in Heaven; looking downward, they observe patterns on Earth; between the two, they observe the myriad things among humankind [?]. They draw the Eight Trigrams to illuminate the Way of yin and yang, devise writing to replace government by knotted cords, make plowing implements to accomplish the work of sowing and reaping, and establish upper and lower garments to make strict the distinctions between superior and inferior. When the people suffer from inadequate dwellings, they erect houses; when difficult terrain obstructs the people, they construct boats and carts; when the people suffer premature death, they introduce medicine; when the people grow accustomed to deceit …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也而權衡以立制器尚象天道明矣作曆
授時人事脩矣體國經野封山濬川而疆
理定矣五典則愼徽之五敎則敬敷之庶
事則明亮之庶類則順成之爲之禮以次
其先後爲之樂以宣其湮鬱害至而爲之
備患生而爲之防凡此皆聖人制作之功
皆道之所在而不可易者也故以一身爲
天下計天下猶一身也以一時爲萬世計
萬世猶一時也由是一人享其利功在一
===
人也遍天下則爲天下之功一世享其利
功在一世也及萬世則爲萬世之功吾見
有八卦而萬世之吉凶以明有書契而萬
世之文字以辨有稼穡而萬世之民食以
足有衣裳而萬世之名分以定居處有方
濟險有具萬世此宮室舟車矣夭死有濟
防僞有道萬世此醫藥權衡矣人時至於
今定也歲功至於今成也五品至於今遜
也百工至於今熙也禮樂至於今和且備
punctuated: 也，而權衡以立。制器尚象，天道明矣；作曆授時，人事脩矣；體國經野，封山濬川，而疆理定矣。五典則愼徽之，五敎則敬敷之，庶事則明亮之，庶類則順成之。爲之禮以次其先後，爲之樂以宣其湮鬱。害至而爲之備，患生而爲之防。凡此皆聖人制作之功，皆道之所在而不可易者也。故以一身爲天下計，天下猶一身也；以一時爲萬世計，萬世猶一時也。由是一人享其利，功在一人也；遍天下，則爲天下之功。一世享其利，功在一世也；及萬世，則爲萬世之功。吾見有八卦而萬世之吉凶以明，有書契而萬世之文字以辨，有稼穡而萬世之民食以足，有衣裳而萬世之名分以定。居處有方，濟險有具，萬世此宮室舟車矣；夭死有濟，防僞有道，萬世此醫藥權衡矣。人時至於今定也，歲功至於今成也，五品至於今遜也，百工至於今熙也，禮樂至於今和且備
translation_en:
…and so balances and steelyards were established. In fashioning implements, the sages esteemed the images, and the Way of Heaven became clear; they made calendars and promulgated the seasons, and human affairs were put in order. They laid out the capital and demarcated the countryside, marked off the mountains and dredged the rivers, and territorial boundaries were settled. They carefully promoted the five constant norms, reverently disseminated the five teachings, clearly administered the many affairs, and brought the myriad kinds of beings to fulfillment in accordance with their natures. They made rites to order precedence and music to give expression to pent-up feelings. They prepared against approaching harm and guarded against emerging troubles. All these were achievements of the sages in creating institutions and implements; in all of them the Way resided, and they could not be altered. Thus, when a single person planned for all under Heaven, all under Heaven was like a single body; when those of one age planned for ten thousand generations, ten thousand generations were like a single age. Accordingly, if one person enjoyed the benefits, the achievement benefited that person; if the benefits extended throughout all under Heaven, it became an achievement for all under Heaven. If one generation enjoyed the benefits, the achievement benefited that generation; if the benefits reached ten thousand generations, it became an achievement for ten thousand generations.

I observe that, with the Eight Trigrams, auspicious and inauspicious outcomes have been made clear for ten thousand generations; with written records, written characters have been distinguished for ten thousand generations; with agriculture, the people's food has been made sufficient for ten thousand generations; and with robes and skirts, distinctions of status have been fixed for ten thousand generations. There are proper means of dwelling and instruments for traversing perilous terrain: for ten thousand generations, these have been palaces and houses, boats and carts. There are remedies against untimely death and means of preventing fraud: for ten thousand generations, these have been medicine and balances and steelyards. The seasons for human activity remain fixed to this day; the year's agricultural work is brought to completion to this day; the five human relationships remain harmonious to this day; the many offices continue to flourish to this day; rites and music remain harmonious and complete to this day…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
也是非聖人之功而何天地至於今位也
日月至於今明也寒暑至於今時也山川
至於今流峙也鳥獸草木昆虫魚鼈至於
今蕃且育也是非聖人之功而何為君者
不能外之以為君為臣者不能外之以為
臣為民者不能外之以為民此其道化之
行天下為公矣萬世為公矣必如是則天
之所以託我者不負民之所以望我者不
孤而我之所以受上天之責亦塞矣五帝
===
有功於天下萬世如此謂非其本於道之
不可易耶是道也循之則治舍之則亂用
之則安舍之則危不可須臾離者也故自
唐虞以來禹因之湯亦因之商不能改乎
夏也湯因之文武亦因之周不能改乎商
也然其報功之典必汲汲於即位之初者
所以扶持培植而躋世道於五帝道化之
中也是五帝之功誠所謂考諸三王而不
謬建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神而無疑百
punctuated: 也。是非聖人之功而何？天地至於今位也，日月至於今明也，寒暑至於今時也，山川至於今流峙也，鳥獸草木昆虫魚鼈至於今蕃且育也。是非聖人之功而何？為君者不能外之以為君，為臣者不能外之以為臣，為民者不能外之以為民。此其道化之行，天下為公矣，萬世為公矣。必如是，則天之所以託我者不負，民之所以望我者不孤，而我之所以受上天之責亦塞矣。五帝有功於天下萬世如此，謂非其本於道之不可易耶？是道也，循之則治，舍之則亂；用之則安，舍之則危，不可須臾離者也。故自唐虞以來，禹因之，湯亦因之，商不能改乎夏也；湯因之，文武亦因之，周不能改乎商也。然其報功之典必汲汲於即位之初者，所以扶持培植而躋世道於五帝道化之中也。是五帝之功，誠所謂「考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百
translation_en:
…If this is not the achievement of the sages, what is it? Heaven and earth remain in their proper places to this day; the sun and moon remain bright; cold and heat arrive in their proper seasons; rivers flow and mountains stand; birds and beasts, plants and trees, insects, fish, and turtles continue to multiply and thrive. If this is not the achievement of the sages, what is it? Rulers cannot rule apart from it; ministers cannot serve apart from it; the people cannot live as the people apart from it. Through the operation of their moral transformation by the Way, its benefits are shared by all under Heaven and by all generations. Only thus will I not betray what Heaven has entrusted to me or disappoint what the people expect of me, and will I discharge the responsibility I have received from Heaven above.

Such were the achievements of the Five Emperors for all under Heaven and for countless generations. Can one say that these were not rooted in the unalterable Way? Following this Way brings order; abandoning it brings disorder. Applying it brings peace; abandoning it brings peril. It cannot be departed from even for an instant. Thus, from the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun onward, Yu followed it, and Tang also followed it: the Shang could not alter what had prevailed under the Xia. Tang followed it, and Kings Wen and Wu also followed it: the Zhou could not alter what had prevailed under the Shang. Yet the rites for recompensing their achievements had to be attended to urgently at the very beginning of a reign, in order to sustain and nurture the moral order of the age and raise it into the sphere of the Five Emperors’ transformation through the Way. The achievements of the Five Emperors truly exemplify the saying: “Tested against the Three Kings, it is without error; established before Heaven and earth, it is without contradiction; examined before ghosts and spirits, it is without doubt; a hundred…”

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
世以俟聖人而不惑者矣奈何自漢而下
爲君者以其功而得位以其功而傳世曾
不得隆其祭祀之典而推其苗裔以封之
於彼夷狄之人無益之敎乃竭力而崇奉
焉果以其有功於天下耶抑以其有功於
萬世耶嗚呼有功者反不若無功者之尊
崇無功者反大過有功者之追慕何其不
思之甚也是雖聖人在天之靈固無望報
之心而君子之論功未免有不可無封其
後之議矣天理民彝其可得而泯滅耶洪
惟我
朝
聖祖神宗誕膺景命叅酌百王脩明祀典思歷
代帝王之功則立廟以崇其祀念群臣謀
謨之績則分配以享其休誠
昭代之盛儀補曠古之缺典也
列聖相承嗣守弗替使天下萬世之人拭目快
覩相忘於大化之中而帝王之道賴以不
punctuated:
世以俟聖人而不惑者矣。奈何自漢而下，爲君者以其功而得位，以其功而傳世，曾不得隆其祭祀之典，而推其苗裔以封之；於彼夷狄之人、無益之敎，乃竭力而崇奉焉。果以其有功於天下耶？抑以其有功於萬世耶？嗚呼！有功者反不若無功者之尊崇，無功者反大過有功者之追慕，何其不思之甚也！是雖聖人在天之靈固無望報之心，而君子之論功，未免有不可無封其後之議矣。天理民彝，其可得而泯滅耶？
洪惟我朝聖祖神宗誕膺景命，叅酌百王，脩明祀典。思歷代帝王之功，則立廟以崇其祀；念群臣謀謨之績，則分配以享其休。誠昭代之盛儀，補曠古之缺典也。列聖相承，嗣守弗替，使天下萬世之人拭目快覩，相忘於大化之中，而帝王之道賴以不
translation_en:
…and can await a sage a hundred generations hence without misgivings. Why, then, have rulers from the Han onward, who gained their thrones and transmitted their rule through the achievements of these sages, failed to enhance the rites of sacrifice to them and seek out their descendants to enfeoff them? Instead, they exert themselves to the utmost in venerating people of foreign tribes and teachings of no benefit. Is this truly because these have rendered service to all under Heaven? Or because they have rendered service to all generations? Alas! Those who have rendered service receive less veneration than those who have rendered none; those without merit receive far greater commemorative devotion than those with merit. How utterly thoughtless! Although the spirits of the sages in Heaven assuredly have no wish for recompense, gentlemen assessing their achievements cannot but argue that their descendants must be enfeoffed. Can Heaven’s principles and the enduring moral norms of the people possibly be obliterated?
We reverently reflect that the sagely founders and divine ancestors of our dynasty received Heaven’s great mandate, weighed the practices of the many kings of antiquity, and restored and clarified the sacrificial rites. Mindful of the achievements of emperors and kings through the ages, they established a temple to honor them with sacrifices; mindful of the accomplishments of their ministers in planning and counsel, they assigned them places to share in the sacrificial honors. These are truly splendid ceremonies of our illustrious age, supplying rites left wanting for ages past. Successive sage sovereigns have maintained this inheritance without neglect, enabling people throughout the realm and for all generations to behold it with delighted eyes and to live so completely within its great transforming influence that they are unaware of it. Through this, the Way of emperors and kings …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
隆所以臻雍熈而基
國家萬億年無疆之休者其精神命脉未必
不本於此也愚以是知繼五帝而有功於
天下萬世端有望於
今日
聖天子
表
擬
勅封宋儒楊時為將樂伯從祀廟庭裔孫謝表
===
鄭閶
同考試官教諭孫批步驟駸駸駢儷不失
異乎諸子之撰
同考試官學正韓批得體
考試官學正周批表佳
考試官教授張批表甚佳觀如此之作
信知其髦士也
伏以
崇儒重道偉乎
punctuated:
隆。所以臻雍熈而基國家萬億年無疆之休者，其精神命脉未必不本於此也。愚以是知，繼五帝而有功於天下萬世，端有望於今日聖天子。

表

擬勅封宋儒楊時為將樂伯、從祀廟庭，裔孫謝表。

鄭閶

同考試官教諭孫批：「步驟駸駸，駢儷不失，異乎諸子之撰。」
同考試官學正韓批：「得體。」
考試官學正周批：「表佳。」
考試官教授張批：「表甚佳。觀如此之作，信知其髦士也。」

伏以：崇儒重道，偉乎
translation_en:
…flourish [?]. The animating spirit and vital force by which harmonious prosperity is attained and the foundation laid for the state's boundless blessings over countless ages may well have their source in this. From this I, in my humble judgment, know that our present sage Son of Heaven may indeed be expected to follow the Five Emperors in rendering service to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations.

Memorial

Draft memorial of thanks by a descendant upon an imperial decree ennobling the Song Confucian scholar Yang Shi as Earl of Jiangle and granting him associated worship in the Confucian temple.

Zheng Chang

Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “The composition advances briskly, maintaining its paired and parallel phrasing. It stands apart from the other candidates' compositions.”
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “Appropriate to the form.”
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “A fine memorial.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “A very fine memorial. On reading a composition such as this, one knows indeed that its author is an outstanding scholar.”

I humbly submit: In honoring Confucian scholars and esteeming the Way, magnificent is …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖德之光列祀追封允矣眞儒之幸典章寔著
禮秩攸加望愜群心光生後裔伏念臣祖
時忝先朝之儒類竊聖學之緒餘苦志窮
經曾立程門之雪潛心體道遠探洙泗之
源得程氏嗣孟子久失之傳倡豫章授晦
庵再傳之學移知三邑惠政在在不忘秉
敎一州人材彬彬輩出文定親承指授以
之而傳春秋南軒上泝淵源因之而闡太
極排靖康之和議國是以張黜王氏之新
===
經淫辭以息傳道功大學者有依衛道力
多儒風克振夫何兩楹夢奠慨徂歲已多
年幸爾一脉道傳覺芳聲如在日歷更世
數未荷
褒嘉顧雖湮晦於前朝敢覬搜揚於
盛世邇者皇華馳至
綸綍渙頒
恩寵賁於先塋光榮及於朽質茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
punctuated: 聖德之光！列祀追封，允矣眞儒之幸。典章寔著，禮秩攸加，望愜群心，光生後裔。伏念臣祖，時忝先朝之儒類，竊聖學之緒餘。苦志窮經，曾立程門之雪；潛心體道，遠探洙泗之源。得程氏嗣孟子久失之傳，倡豫章授晦庵再傳之學。移知三邑，惠政在在不忘；秉敎一州，人材彬彬輩出。文定親承指授，以之而傳春秋；南軒上泝淵源，因之而闡太極。排靖康之和議，國是以張；黜王氏之新經，淫辭以息。傳道功大，學者有依；衛道力多，儒風克振。夫何兩楹夢奠，慨徂歲已多年！幸爾一脉道傳，覺芳聲如在日。歷更世數，未荷褒嘉。顧雖湮晦於前朝，敢覬搜揚於盛世。邇者皇華馳至，綸綍渙頒，恩寵賁於先塋，光榮及於朽質。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇
translation_en:
…the radiance of Your Majesty’s sagely virtue! Inclusion among those receiving ritual sacrifices and the posthumous bestowal of a title are truly blessings for a genuine Confucian. The ceremonial provisions have been clearly established, and ritual honors conferred. These fulfill the hopes of all and bring glory to his descendants.

I humbly reflect that my ancestor once had the honor of belonging to the Confucian scholars of a former dynasty and received a portion of the legacy of sagely learning. Resolutely devoting himself to fathoming the Classics, he once stood in the snow at Cheng’s gate; concentrating his mind on embodying the Way, he traced its distant source to the Zhu and Si rivers. He received from Master Cheng the transmission that continued the teaching of Mencius after it had long been lost, and promoted the learning transmitted through Yuzhang to Hui’an in the second generation. Serving successively as magistrate of three counties, he left benevolent administrations remembered everywhere; directing education in a prefecture, he brought forth successive cohorts of cultivated men of talent. Wending personally received his instruction and used it to transmit the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals; Nanxuan traced the teaching upstream to its source and thereby elucidated the Supreme Ultimate. He opposed proposals for peace during the Jingkang era, thereby upholding proper state policy; he rejected Master Wang’s new interpretations of the Classics, thereby silencing wayward doctrines. His achievements in transmitting the Way were great, giving scholars something on which to rely; his efforts to defend the Way were considerable, enabling the Confucian tradition to flourish.

Alas, why did he have to dream of offerings set between the two pillars—the omen of his death? We lament that so many years have passed! Fortunately, the single thread transmitting the Way has endured, and his good reputation seems as vivid as when he was alive. Several generations have passed without his receiving imperial commendation. Though he remained obscure under the preceding dynasty, I ventured to hope that he would be sought out and honored in this flourishing age. Recently, imperial envoys hastened here, and Your Majesty’s decree was generously promulgated. Imperial favor adorned my ancestor’s grave, and its glory reached even my own decrepit person. This, I humbly submit, is because we have been fortunate to encounter 〇〇〇〇…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
睿資天縱
聖德日新運撫盈成克紹
祖宗之大業心勤惕厲率循帝王之宏規事惟
切於斯文禮特隆於吾道
恩覃遠近無小善而或遺諫納忠良不邇言而
見鄙華夷載德中外歸心念臣祖有宋遺
賢爵名未稱因邇臣疏章
上請曲賜追崇將樂伯封遡支流於生長之地
東廡位列別授受於先後之倫依大聖之
===
門墻衣冠有耀與先賢之廟食俎豆增輝
天澤洊加雲仍感幸蔀屋普中天之照寒谷回
復晝之春起北學之文風上聯伊洛昌南
傳之道氣下貫考亭誠忭誠懽載歌載頌
德齊罔極顧填海以何功
壽等無疆效呼嵩而徒切惟冀推明夙學繼
述儒宗躋斯世於昇平致吾
君於熈皞河清海晏見三五帝王之休徵地久
天長垂億萬斯年之丕緒臣下情無任瞻
punctuated: 睿資天縱，聖德日新，運撫盈成，克紹祖宗之大業；心勤惕厲，率循帝王之宏規。事惟切於斯文，禮特隆於吾道。恩覃遠近，無小善而或遺；諫納忠良，不邇言而見鄙。華夷載德，中外歸心。念臣祖有宋遺賢，爵名未稱，因邇臣疏章上請，曲賜追崇。將樂伯封，遡支流於生長之地；東廡位列，別授受於先後之倫。依大聖之門墻，衣冠有耀；與先賢之廟食，俎豆增輝。天澤洊加，雲仍感幸。蔀屋普中天之照，寒谷回復晝之春。起北學之文風，上聯伊洛；昌南傳之道氣，下貫考亭。誠忭誠懽，載歌載頌。德齊罔極，顧填海以何功；壽等無疆，效呼嵩而徒切。惟冀推明夙學，繼述儒宗，躋斯世於昇平，致吾君於熈皞。河清海晏，見三五帝王之休徵；地久天長，垂億萬斯年之丕緒。臣下情無任瞻
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s sagely gifts are Heaven-bestowed, and your sacred virtue is renewed daily. Presiding over an age of fullness and accomplishment, you worthily continue the great enterprise of your ancestors; diligent and vigilant at heart, you follow the grand precepts of emperors and kings. Your undertakings show particular concern for this cultural tradition, and your ritual honors especially exalt our Way. Your grace extends far and near, overlooking no good deed, however small; you accept remonstrance from loyal and worthy men, disdaining no words for their humble familiarity. Chinese and foreign peoples alike cherish your virtue; those within and beyond the realm give you their allegiance.

Mindful that my ancestor was a worthy man of the former Song whose title and rank did not adequately reflect his stature, you responded to a memorial submitted by an attendant minister and graciously bestowed posthumous honors. His enfeoffment as Earl of Jiangle traces the tributary stream back to the place where he was born and grew up; his placement in the eastern cloister distinguishes the sequence of those who transmitted and received the teaching. Within the precincts of the Great Sage, his cap and robes shine with honor; sharing the temple offerings of earlier worthies, his sacrificial vessels gain added splendor. Heaven’s bounty is bestowed repeatedly, and his distant descendants gratefully rejoice in their good fortune. Even darkened dwellings share the light of the sun at its zenith, and the cold valley regains the spring of returning daylight [?]. You revive the scholarly influence of northern learning, linking it back to the Yi and Luo rivers, and foster the vital force of the Way transmitted southward, carrying it onward to Kaoting.

Truly delighted and truly joyful, we sing and offer praise. Your virtue is boundless: what could our efforts to fill the sea accomplish in return? May your longevity likewise know no bounds; we can only fervently emulate the cries of acclamation at Mount Song. We hope only to elucidate what we have long studied and carry forward the teachings of the masters of Confucian learning, bringing this age to peace and prosperity and our sovereign to radiant harmony. With the Yellow River clear and the seas tranquil, may we witness the auspicious signs of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors; enduring as earth and heaven, may your great enterprise descend through countless millions of years. Your servant, overcome by his feelings, gazes upward…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
謝廷瑞
===
同考試官教諭孫批策問正以觀士子之
才識此策條答無餘鋪叙停當如三峽倒流一
瀉千里波濤湧躍抑揚起伏自有可觀者且歸
美
聖朝制作之盛道洽臣民德敷天下至精至純有非歷代可擬他日
捷春魁對
大廷敷摠
聖化又必非今日之作其闈中才識之士也歟是宜高薦
同考試官學正韓批推尊得宜真識文字
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至。謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲
策
第一問
謝廷瑞
同考試官教諭孫批：策問正以觀士子之才識。此策條答無餘，鋪叙停當，如三峽倒流，一瀉千里，波濤湧躍，抑揚起伏，自有可觀者。且歸美聖朝制作之盛，道洽臣民，德敷天下，至精至純，有非歷代可擬。他日捷春魁，對大廷，敷摠聖化，又必非今日之作。其闈中才識之士也歟！是宜高薦。
同考試官學正韓批：推尊得宜，真識文字
translation_en:
…gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and reverent awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Xie Tingrui
Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: Policy questions serve precisely to reveal candidates’ ability and discernment. This essay answers every point, leaving nothing unaddressed; its exposition is aptly arranged. Like the waters of the Three Gorges surging in reverse and pouring a thousand li in a single rush, its waves leap and surge; its modulations, rises, and falls are well worth observing. Moreover, it attributes due praise to the flourishing institutions of the sage dynasty: its Way permeates officials and people, and its virtue spreads throughout the realm. These are supremely refined and pure, beyond comparison with those of successive earlier dynasties. When, in days to come, he wins highest honors in the spring examination, responds at the imperial court, and expounds comprehensively upon Your Majesty’s transforming influence, his writing will surely surpass even today’s work. Is he not a man of ability and discernment among the candidates in this examination compound? He deserves a high recommendation.
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: His expressions of reverence and praise are fitting; he truly understands literary composition…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
者
考試官學正周批策善答
考試官教授張批條答甚詳善鋪
昭代制作之盛
一原妙用前代肇開心學之源千載神交
當代遠承心學之統孟子曰先聖後聖其揆
一也漢唐宋諸君類無墳典之學率墜文
墨之中於道旣遠而治日離其視古今聖
人心學之著制作之盛奚可同日而語哉
===
執事發策以此詢承學蓋欲天下知遵
一王之制彰大一統之盛也請槩陳之有一
代之興則有一代之制而文字又制之所
當先者故虞夏商周之盛帝舜有明良之
歌大禹有洛書之數伊尹有風愆之戒文
王有重易之篇此皆聖人之文經緯天地
軌範帝王者也後世漢高祖徒以英雄之
資素無詩書之澤大風猛士句非不壯麗
也而尊賢尚德之意微唐太宗親躬汗馬
punctuated:
者。
考試官學正周批：策善答。
考試官教授張批：條答甚詳，善鋪昭代制作之盛。
一原妙用，前代肇開心學之源；千載神交，當代遠承心學之統。孟子曰：「先聖後聖，其揆一也。」漢唐宋諸君，類無墳典之學，率墜文墨之中，於道旣遠，而治日離。其視古今聖人心學之著、制作之盛，奚可同日而語哉？
執事發策，以此詢承學，蓋欲天下知遵一王之制，彰大一統之盛也。請槩陳之。有一代之興，則有一代之制，而文字又制之所當先者。故虞夏商周之盛，帝舜有明良之歌，大禹有洛書之數，伊尹有風愆之戒，文王有重易之篇。此皆聖人之文，經緯天地、軌範帝王者也。後世漢高祖徒以英雄之資，素無詩書之澤，大風猛士句非不壯麗也，而尊賢尚德之意微。唐太宗親躬汗馬
translation_en:
…one who is such.
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “The policy question is well answered.”
Examiner Zhang, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: “The responses to the individual points are very detailed, and ably expound the flourishing institutions and compositions of our illustrious dynasty.”
Wondrous operation from a single source: in an earlier age, the source of the learning of the mind was first opened. Spiritual communion across a thousand years: in the present age, the succession of the learning of the mind has been received from the distant past. Mengzi said: “The earlier sages and the later sages followed the same standard.” The rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song generally lacked learning in the ancient canonical writings and mostly became engrossed in literary composition. Already distant from the Way, their government departed from it further each day. How could they be spoken of in the same breath as the manifest learning of the mind and the flourishing institutions and compositions of the sages, ancient and modern?
You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question to inquire of us students about this, surely wishing all under Heaven to know that they should follow the institutions of a single sovereign and to make manifest the grandeur of supreme unity. Allow me to set this out in broad terms. Whenever a dynasty arises, it has its own institutions, and writing is among the foremost matters to be established. Thus, in the flourishing ages of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, Emperor Shun had his song of the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers; the Great Yu had the numbers of the Luo River Writing; Yi Yin had his admonitions concerning pernicious customs and faults; and King Wen had his text on the doubled hexagrams of the Changes. These were all writings of sages, ordering Heaven and Earth and providing models for emperors and kings.
In later ages, Gaozu of Han possessed merely the natural endowments of a hero and had never been nurtured by the Odes and Documents. His lines about the great wind and mighty warriors were certainly magnificent, but expressed little intention of honoring the worthy and esteeming virtue. Taizong of Tang personally engaged in the exertions of mounted warfare…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之旁垂情經史之術宮體帝範言非不激
切也而正身率物之意寡漢武帝之朱雁
歌白麟歌唐玄宗之孝經序三傑詩以至
宋太祖華山日出之章太宗宮花臘雪之
句不過宣一時之驕心著紙上之陳迹求
諸帝王繼天立極之本原安國保民之學
術安在哉庖犧神農有龍書穗書之作神
堯伯禹有龜書鍾鼎之作薤書鳥書非湯
文之作乎此皆制起一心神妙萬化者也
===
後世漢光武工一札披心腹於萬里以法
則英偉矣唐太宗精飛白致責望於臣鄰
以制則遒勁矣灑翰金鑾無愧於淮南之
書者唐德宗也寄懷翰墨滌煩於盈尺之
字者宋太宗也太宗澄神靜慮而得學書
之法高宗清心寡慾而得寫書之妙率皆
留心小技而亡心於大學銳意細娛而忽
意於遠圖求諸帝王民淳事簡之規模玉
帛衣裳之影響安在哉文盛於虞夏商周
punctuated:
之旁，垂情經史之術，《宮體》《帝範》，言非不激切也，而正身率物之意寡。漢武帝之《朱雁歌》《白麟歌》，唐玄宗之《孝經序》《三傑詩》，以至宋太祖《華山日出》之章、太宗《宮花》《臘雪》之句，不過宣一時之驕心，著紙上之陳迹。求諸帝王繼天立極之本原、安國保民之學術，安在哉？

庖犧、神農有龍書、穗書之作，神堯、伯禹有龜書、鍾鼎之作，薤書、鳥書非湯、文之作乎？此皆制起一心，神妙萬化者也。後世漢光武工一札，披心腹於萬里，以法則英偉矣；唐太宗精飛白，致責望於臣鄰，以制則遒勁矣。灑翰金鑾，無愧於淮南之書者，唐德宗也；寄懷翰墨，滌煩於盈尺之字者，宋太宗也。太宗澄神靜慮而得學書之法，高宗清心寡慾而得寫書之妙，率皆留心小技而亡心於大學，銳意細娛而忽意於遠圖。求諸帝王民淳事簡之規模、玉帛衣裳之影響，安在哉？

文盛於虞夏商周
translation_en:
…amid his military exertions, he devoted attention to the learning of the classics and histories. In “Palace Style” [?] and “Models for Emperors,” his words were certainly impassioned and earnest, yet showed little concern for rectifying himself and thereby setting an example for others. Emperor Wu of Han’s “Song of the Vermilion Goose” and “Song of the White Qilin,” Emperor Xuanzong of Tang’s “Preface to the Classic of Filial Piety” and “Poem on the Three Worthies,” and even Emperor Taizu of Song’s verses on sunrise over Mount Hua and Emperor Taizong’s lines on palace flowers and year-end snow did no more than proclaim a passing mood of pride and leave stale traces upon paper. Where in these can one find the foundations by which emperors and kings carry on Heaven’s work and establish the supreme standard, or the learning by which they secure the state and protect the people?

Paoxi and Shennong created dragon script and grain-ear script; the divine Yao and Bo Yu created tortoise script and bell-and-cauldron script. Were not scallion-leaf script and bird script the creations of Tang and King Wen? These were all forms devised within a single mind, wondrously embodying myriad transformations. In later ages, Emperor Guangwu of Han was accomplished in writing letters, laying bare his heart to recipients ten thousand li away: judged by calligraphic method, his work was indeed heroic and magnificent. Emperor Taizong of Tang excelled in “flying-white” script, conveying his admonitions and expectations to his close ministers: judged by its form, his work was indeed vigorous and forceful. It was Emperor Dezong of Tang who wielded his brush in the Jinluan Hall, producing calligraphy worthy of comparison with that of Huainan. It was Emperor Taizong of Song who entrusted his feelings to brush and ink, dispelling his cares through characters a full foot in size. Taizong clarified his spirit and stilled his thoughts, thereby acquiring the method for learning calligraphy; Gaozong purified his mind and reduced his desires, thereby attaining the subtleties of writing. Yet all these rulers generally devoted their minds to a minor skill while losing sight of the Great Learning, eagerly pursuing trifling amusements while neglecting far-reaching plans. Where in their work can one find the pattern of imperial and royal government under which the people were unspoiled and affairs uncomplicated, or the influence of rule through the rites of jade and silk and the ceremonial robes of office?

Literary composition flourished under Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
書妙於五帝三王漢唐宋不得而並美矣
洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝上紹聖神心學之傳下正華夏人
文之統條成
大誥三編定爲洪武正韻于以新天下之耳目
一天下之心志繼以
太宗文皇帝孝順事實爲善陰隲
宣宗章皇帝五倫書
===
英宗睿皇帝大明一統志
憲宗純皇帝續資治通鑑綱目造端託始聿開
萬世太平之基累洽重熙式闡六經文明
之治詩書禮澤文遍華夷點畫形象字同
朝野置斯民於文物之內納天下於
皇極之中而雍熙泰和之世端在
今日盛矣哉我
朝之制作乎其載道之文字有得於
聖神傳心之妙用乎區區漢唐宋諸作安得而
punctuated:
書妙於五帝三王，漢唐宋不得而並美矣。
洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，上紹聖神心學之傳，下正華夏人文之統，條成《大誥》三編，定爲《洪武正韻》，于以新天下之耳目，一天下之心志。繼以太宗文皇帝《孝順事實》《爲善陰隲》，宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，英宗睿皇帝《大明一統志》，憲宗純皇帝《續資治通鑑綱目》，造端託始，聿開萬世太平之基；累洽重熙，式闡六經文明之治。詩書禮澤，文遍華夷；點畫形象，字同朝野。置斯民於文物之內，納天下於皇極之中，而雍熙泰和之世，端在今日。盛矣哉，我朝之制作乎！其載道之文字，有得於聖神傳心之妙用乎！區區漢唐宋諸作，安得而
translation_en:
…calligraphy attained its excellence under the Five Emperors and Three Kings; the Han, Tang, and Song could not rival their beauty.
We reverently reflect that our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao carried forward from above the transmission of the sages’ and divine rulers’ learning of the mind, and rectified below the cultural succession of the Chinese realm. He set forth the Great Pronouncements (Da Gao) in three compilations and established the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Era (Hongwu Zhengyun), thereby renewing the eyes and ears of all under Heaven and unifying their minds and purposes. These were followed by Emperor Taizong Wen’s True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi) and Doing Good and Its Hidden Recompense (Weishan Yinzhi); Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun Shu); Emperor Yingzong Rui’s Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming Yitong Zhi); and Emperor Xianzong Chun’s Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Xu Zizhi Tongjian Gangmu). By establishing these beginnings, they laid the foundation for peace lasting ten thousand generations. Through successive ages of concord and prosperity, they manifested the enlightened governance of the Six Classics. Through the beneficent influence of the Odes, Documents, and rites, culture extended throughout Chinese and non-Chinese lands; in their dots, strokes, shapes, and forms, written characters were uniform at court and among the people. They placed the people within the sphere of cultural refinement and brought all under Heaven within the imperial standard. An age of harmony, prosperity, and perfect peace is indeed here today. How magnificent are the institutions and works of our dynasty! Surely its writings, which convey the Way, have grasped the wondrous workings of the transmission of the mind by sages and divine rulers! How could the paltry works of the Han, Tang, and Song possibly …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
彷彿之哉謹述以對
第二問
金文明
同考試官教諭周批史策存疑固當有辯
然於風簷寸晷之下剖析無遺且以公正立論
誠有識見之士也高薦允宜
同考試官教諭徐批集議一策正氣凛然
而忠愛之心每著他日立
朝其丰采能無動人者
===
同考試官教諭徐批參可否於衆論决得
失於一心則天下無難處之事矣此作得之
考試官學正周批足見學識
考試官教授張批有鋪叙且事實不遺
其善答策者
對有持正之議論而後可以慮天下之大
事有至公之平决而後可以成天下之大
事蓋立議不正則意向所趨或激或隨而
無以公天下之是非决議非公則喜怒所
punctuated:
彷彿之哉？謹述以對。

第二問
金文明

同考試官教諭周批：史策存疑，固當有辯。然於風簷寸晷之下，剖析無遺，且以公正立論，誠有識見之士也。高薦允宜。

同考試官教諭徐批：集議一策，正氣凛然，而忠愛之心每著。他日立朝，其丰采能無動人者？

同考試官教諭徐批：參可否於衆論，决得失於一心，則天下無難處之事矣。此作得之。

考試官學正周批：足見學識。

考試官教授張批：有鋪叙，且事實不遺，其善答策者。

對：有持正之議論，而後可以慮天下之大事；有至公之平决，而後可以成天下之大事。蓋立議不正，則意向所趨，或激或隨，而無以公天下之是非；决議非公，則喜怒所
translation_en:
…even remotely resemble them? I respectfully set this forth in reply.

Second Question
Jin Wenming

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Doubtful points in historical records certainly call for debate. Yet to analyze them exhaustively under the wind-swept eaves and within the brief time allotted, and moreover to base one’s argument on fairness and impartiality—this truly marks a man of discernment. A high recommendation is entirely fitting.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: This policy essay on collective deliberation is imposing in its moral rectitude, and repeatedly reveals a heart of loyalty and devotion. When he takes his place at court in days to come, how could his bearing fail to move others?

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Weighing approval and objection among the many opinions, and deciding their merits and faults within a single mind: with this, no affair in the realm will be difficult to handle. This composition grasps that principle.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Ample evidence of learning and discernment.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: The exposition is fully developed, and no relevant facts are omitted. He is indeed skilled at answering policy questions.

Reply: Only when deliberations uphold what is right can the great affairs of the realm be considered; only when judgments are equitable and wholly impartial can the great affairs of the realm be accomplished. For if the positions advanced in deliberation are not upright, one’s inclinations will tend either toward excessive vehemence or toward acquiescence, leaving no means to judge impartially what is right and wrong in the realm. If decisions upon deliberations are not impartial, then what joy and anger…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
發或撓或回而無以一廟堂之議論立之
者正而决之者公則天下無難處之事豈
不足以成天下之大事哉請因明問而陳
之唐子西辨同論有曰人主駕馭群臣正
恐其雷同陳公輔尚同論亦曰群臣無可
否未有能致治者是則謀之貴多議之貴
博也但恐唯唯為同者未免於逢迎遷就
之議而嘵嘵為異者又墮於求勝已私之
偏則斷而决之又在於君心之公耳三代
===
而上君臣都俞吁咈於一堂之上固無可
辨自漢而下上下互持其私說以求勝則
不能無可疑者韓安國之議匈奴利害非
不明也而王恢以私說勝之不然何以有
馬邑之禍趙充國之議屯田養軍非無益
也而朝議以不便阻之若爾何以成屯田
之功延國祚而久安長治蕭瑀封建之論
是矣奈何唐魏徵欲阻其議而進五不可
之說使先王道不行於唐者是以魏鄭公
punctuated: 發，或撓或回，而無以一廟堂之議論。立之者正，而决之者公，則天下無難處之事，豈不足以成天下之大事哉？請因明問而陳之。唐子西《辨同論》有曰：「人主駕馭群臣，正恐其雷同。」陳公輔《尚同論》亦曰：「群臣無可否，未有能致治者。」是則謀之貴多，議之貴博也。但恐唯唯為同者，未免於逢迎遷就之議；而嘵嘵為異者，又墮於求勝已私之偏。則斷而决之，又在於君心之公耳。三代而上，君臣都俞吁咈於一堂之上，固無可辨。自漢而下，上下互持其私說以求勝，則不能無可疑者。韓安國之議匈奴，利害非不明也，而王恢以私說勝之。不然，何以有馬邑之禍？趙充國之議屯田養軍，非無益也，而朝議以不便阻之。若爾，何以成屯田之功，延國祚而久安長治？蕭瑀封建之論，是矣。奈何唐魏徵欲阻其議，而進五不可之說，使先王道不行於唐者，是以魏鄭公
translation_en:
…are expressed, they may yield to pressure or turn aside, leaving no means to unify deliberations at court. If those who formulate proposals are upright and those who decide upon them are impartial, there will be no affairs in the realm that are difficult to handle. Would this not suffice to accomplish the great affairs of the realm? Allow me to set this forth in response to your discerning question.

Tang Zixi says in his Discourse on Distinguishing Agreement: “When the ruler directs his ministers, what he particularly fears is their unthinking agreement.” Chen Gongfu likewise says in his Discourse on Esteeming Agreement: “When ministers neither approve nor disapprove, none has ever been able to bring about good government.” Thus, in planning, numerous proposals are valuable, and in deliberation, breadth of discussion is valuable. Yet there is reason to fear that those who assent with repeated expressions of agreement cannot escape offering views that flatter and accommodate, while those who noisily dissent fall into the partiality of seeking victory for their own private interests [?]. Judgment and decision therefore depend, in turn, upon the impartiality of the ruler’s mind.

In the Three Dynasties and earlier, rulers and ministers voiced approval and dissent together in a single hall; there was surely nothing requiring dispute. From the Han onward, however, sovereigns and ministers each clung to their private views and sought to prevail, so there could not but be grounds for doubt. Han Anguo’s deliberation concerning the Xiongnu was by no means unclear about the advantages and dangers, yet Wang Hui prevailed over him with his private view. Otherwise, how could the disaster at Mayi have occurred? Zhao Chongguo’s proposal to establish agricultural colonies to provision the army was by no means without benefit, yet deliberations at court obstructed it on grounds of impracticality. If that were so, how could the agricultural colonies have achieved their success, prolonging the dynasty’s tenure and securing enduring peace and good government?

Xiao Yu’s argument for establishing hereditary fiefs was correct. Why, then, did Wei Zheng of the Tang seek to obstruct his proposal by advancing five reasons against it, preventing the Way of the former kings from being practiced under the Tang? Thus Wei, Duke of Zheng…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
不能有違顏師古之廷議也父不受誅而
子復仇公羊春秋之義明矣奈何陳子昻
欲誅元慶而有表其閭之議使義與法而
不相悖者是以陳子昻不能不來柳子厚
之駁議也議靈州之棄守當以輔臣之言
爲是而李沆楊億之言爲非蓋靈州不可
棄也議綏州之城否當以孫全照之言爲
是而洪湛之言爲非蓋綏州不可城也夫
建明公議在士夫之衆見主張公議在人
===
主之一心昔者孫權曾斫案以拒迎操之
議遂有赤壁之捷晉武曾推枰以决平吳
之議乃有降吳之功夫孫權僭僞之主耳
晉武偏安之君耳能定議而成功如此况
以天下之大君主天下之大事於群議而
能定者尚何功之不可成哉不然則一可
一否雅鄭亂於聽納而可否無以斷也一
是一非朱紫眩於視瞻而是非無以辨也
甚者借一是之名箝百家之口如指鹿爲
punctuated:
不能有違顏師古之廷議也。父不受誅而子復仇，《公羊春秋》之義明矣。奈何陳子昻欲誅元慶，而有表其閭之議？使義與法而不相悖者，是以陳子昻不能不來柳子厚之駁議也。議靈州之棄守，當以輔臣之言爲是，而李沆、楊億之言爲非，蓋靈州不可棄也。議綏州之城否，當以孫全照之言爲是，而洪湛之言爲非，蓋綏州不可城也。夫建明公議，在士夫之衆見；主張公議，在人主之一心。
昔者孫權曾斫案以拒迎操之議，遂有赤壁之捷；晉武曾推枰以决平吳之議，乃有降吳之功。夫孫權，僭僞之主耳；晉武，偏安之君耳。能定議而成功如此，况以天下之大君，主天下之大事，於群議而能定者，尚何功之不可成哉？不然，則一可一否，雅鄭亂於聽納，而可否無以斷也；一是一非，朱紫眩於視瞻，而是非無以辨也。甚者，借一是之名，箝百家之口，如指鹿爲
translation_en:
…could not contravene Yan Shigu’s deliberation at court. When a father has been put to death unjustly, his son may avenge him: the principle set forth in the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals is clear. Why, then, did Chen Zi’ang wish to execute Yuanqing while also proposing that his neighborhood gate be marked in his honor? The aim was to prevent righteousness and law from conflicting [?]; thus Chen Zi’ang could not but invite Liu Zihou’s rebuttal. In deliberating whether to abandon or defend Lingzhou, the words of the chief ministers should be judged right, and those of Li Hang and Yang Yi wrong, for Lingzhou could not be abandoned. In deliberating whether to fortify Suizhou, Sun Quanzhao’s words should be judged right, and Hong Zhan’s wrong, for Suizhou should not be fortified. Establishing and elucidating impartial counsel rests on the collective judgment of scholar-officials; upholding it rests on the single mind of the ruler.
Formerly, Sun Quan struck his desk with a sword to reject the proposal to submit to Cao Cao, and consequently won the victory at Chibi. Emperor Wu of Jin once pushed aside his game board to settle the proposal to conquer Wu, and consequently secured Wu’s surrender. Sun Quan was merely an illegitimate ruler, and Emperor Wu of Jin merely a sovereign content to rule one part of the realm. If they could settle deliberations and achieve such success, how much more could the great sovereign of all under Heaven, presiding over the great affairs of the realm! If he can reach a firm decision amid competing counsels, what achievement could remain beyond his grasp? Otherwise, with one voice approving and another opposing, the orthodox music of the court and the licentious music of Zheng become confused in what he hears and accepts, and he cannot decide what to approve or reject. With one voice declaring something right and another wrong, vermilion and purple bewilder his sight, and he cannot distinguish right from wrong. Worse still, someone may invoke the claim that one view alone is right to silence every other school of thought, as in pointing to a deer and calling it…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
馬者豈一朝一夕之故哉惟度以吾心之
拳則事之輕重莫逃量以本然之度則事
之長短盡識而又以理察之以義處之以
時拳之則懸百鍊以照眾說之姸媸雖欲
掩而不可得矣尚何天下之事不可處天
下之事不可成哉寡昧之見聊以復明問
之萬一未知是否
第三問
林士元
===
同考試官學正侯批昌黎嘗以一事不知
為儒者之耻此策博洽無遺其能無愧於儒者
矣乎
考試官學正周批太極圖諸書為理學
之宗正吾儒所當講者此策詞與事稱讀之猶
可想見聖賢當時氣象是宜錄出
考試官敎授張批分析甚明非理學之
士不能也
對知聖賢妙道之所存當知聖賢妙道之
punctuated:
馬者，豈一朝一夕之故哉？惟度以吾心之拳，則事之輕重莫逃；量以本然之度，則事之長短盡識。而又以理察之，以義處之，以時拳之，則懸百鍊以照眾說之姸媸，雖欲掩而不可得矣。尚何天下之事不可處，天下之事不可成哉？寡昧之見，聊以復明問之萬一，未知是否。
第三問
林士元
同考試官學正侯批：昌黎嘗以一事不知為儒者之耻。此策博洽無遺，其能無愧於儒者矣乎？
考試官學正周批：《太極圖》諸書為理學之宗，正吾儒所當講者。此策詞與事稱，讀之猶可想見聖賢當時氣象，是宜錄出。
考試官敎授張批：分析甚明，非理學之士不能也。
對：知聖賢妙道之所存，當知聖賢妙道之
translation_en:
…a horse—could such a situation have arisen in a single day or evening? Only by weighing matters with the balance of my own mind [?] can their relative importance never escape me; by measuring them against their inherent standard, I can fully discern their strengths and shortcomings. If I further examine them through principle, deal with them according to righteousness, and weigh them according to the circumstances of the time [?], this is like hanging up a mirror refined a hundred times to reveal the beauty and ugliness of the various opinions: even those wishing to conceal these qualities cannot do so. What affair under Heaven could then not be managed, and what undertaking under Heaven could not be accomplished? With these unenlightened views, I venture to answer one ten-thousandth of your discerning question, uncertain whether they are correct.
Third Question
Lin Shiyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Hou, School Instructor: Changli [Han Yu] once regarded ignorance of even a single matter as a disgrace to a Confucian scholar. This policy essay is broadly learned and comprehensive, leaving nothing out. Surely its author can stand without shame among Confucian scholars?
Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: The Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and the other works are foundational texts of the Learning of Principle, precisely what we Confucian scholars ought to study and discuss. In this policy essay, the language is commensurate with the subject matter. Reading it, one can still envision the bearing of the sages and worthies in their own day. It deserves to be selected for inclusion in the record.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The analysis is exceptionally clear. Only a scholar of the Learning of Principle could achieve this.
Response: To understand where the wondrous Way of the sages and worthies resides, one must understand the wondrous Way of the sages and worthies in its…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
所發夫始終本末而一以貫之者聖賢妙
道之所存太極之所以爲圖也或主理或
主數或主氣各有攸當而又未嘗不相爲
表裏羽翼者聖賢妙道之所發太極先天
之圖論氣之章也後之學者於其妙道之
發率意以優劣之固不可而況妙道之存
包羅始終兼總本末者而可以一偏之見
肆爲是紛紛之說以議之哉執事發策以
太極圖諸說諸書之同異得失下詢愚雖
===
不敏未敢諉諸性與天道不可得而聞也
姑陳其槩以復夫自堯舜周文之響息孔
曾思孟之迹蕪更秦及漢歷唐至宋星聚
奎而文風丕振水泝洛而道統流傳時則
有若周子者出玉淵金井其志慮也霽月
光風其胸次也獨得千載不傳之秘於殘
篇斷簡之中而有太極圖作焉推本無極
而太極太極而兩儀兩儀而五氣五氣而
四時剖析幽微根極領要至矣盡矣所謂
punctuated:
所發。夫始終本末而一以貫之者，聖賢妙道之所存，太極之所以爲圖也。或主理，或主數，或主氣，各有攸當，而又未嘗不相爲表裏羽翼者，聖賢妙道之所發，太極、先天之圖、論氣之章也。後之學者，於其妙道之發，率意以優劣之，固不可；而況妙道之存，包羅始終，兼總本末者，而可以一偏之見，肆爲是紛紛之說以議之哉？執事發策，以太極圖諸說諸書之同異得失下詢，愚雖不敏，未敢諉諸性與天道不可得而聞也。姑陳其槩以復。
夫自堯舜周文之響息，孔曾思孟之迹蕪，更秦及漢，歷唐至宋，星聚奎而文風丕振，水泝洛而道統流傳。時則有若周子者出，玉淵金井，其志慮也；霽月光風，其胸次也。獨得千載不傳之秘於殘篇斷簡之中，而有太極圖作焉。推本無極而太極，太極而兩儀，兩儀而五氣，五氣而四時，剖析幽微，根極領要，至矣，盡矣！所謂：
translation_en:
…the manifestation of the sages’ wondrous Way. That which runs as a single thread through beginning and end, root and branch, is where the sages’ wondrous Way resides; this is why the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate was made. Some accounts emphasize principle, others number, and others vital force (qi). Each has its appropriate application, yet they invariably complement and support one another. These are manifestations of the sages’ wondrous Way: the diagrams of the Supreme Ultimate and Prior Heaven, and the chapter discussing vital force. Later scholars certainly must not arbitrarily rank these manifestations of the wondrous Way as superior or inferior. How much less may they, taking a one-sided view, recklessly advance these conflicting arguments to criticize that in which the wondrous Way resides, encompassing beginning and end and embracing root and branch alike? You, sir, have posed a policy question, graciously asking about the similarities and differences, merits and shortcomings, of the various explanations and writings concerning the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. Though dull-witted, I dare not evade the question by pleading that human nature and the Way of Heaven cannot be heard of. Let me offer an outline in reply.
After the echoes of Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and King Wen had fallen silent, and the traces of Confucius, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius had become overgrown, time passed through Qin and Han, through Tang, and down to Song. The stars gathered in the constellation Kui, and literary culture flourished greatly; the waters were traced upstream to the Luo River, and the succession of the Way continued to flow. It was then that a man such as Master Zhou emerged. His aspirations and reflections were like a jade pool and a golden well; his inner disposition was like the moon after rain and a clear, gentle breeze. Alone, amid fragmentary texts and broken bamboo slips, he grasped the secret that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years, and thus produced the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. Tracing things to their source, he proceeded from the Limitless to the Supreme Ultimate, from the Supreme Ultimate to the Two Modes, from the Two Modes to the five vital forces, and from the five vital forces to the four seasons. He analyzed the hidden and subtle, plumbed the ultimate roots, and grasped the essentials. How consummate! How exhaustive! As it is said, …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
先生之精因圖以示先生之蘊因圖以發
尚奚疑耶然而難者乃謂其不當以繼善
成性分陰陽殊不知變化無窮而稟受有
定其動靜之分昭如也乃謂其不當以太
極陰陽分道器殊不知太極無象而陰陽
有氣其上下之别秩如也仁義中正固不
可以體用言然誠通誠復各有所屬體用
是何傷哉體用一源固不可以先後論然
舉理舉事兩無所嫌先後不其然乎圖之
===
論仁參之以中正類之以陰陽剛柔則不
得為專言之仁矣偏指陽動之議誠有所
未宜仁義中正屬之以動靜配之以元亨
利貞則脉絡分明非支離穿鑿矣分反其
類之說誠有所未當不由師傳獨得秘傳
之旨是也誌文足以為此圖之明驗种穆
之學烏足以語此立象盡意示發精蘊之
言是也通書所以闡此圖之蘊奧先生之
學將奚以加此廣大詳備太極之規模方
punctuated: 先生之精因圖以示，先生之蘊因圖以發」，尚奚疑耶？然而難者乃謂其不當以繼善、成性分陰陽，殊不知變化無窮而稟受有定，其動靜之分昭如也。乃謂其不當以太極、陰陽分道器，殊不知太極無象而陰陽有氣，其上下之别秩如也。仁義中正固不可以體用言，然誠通、誠復各有所屬，體用是何傷哉？體用一源固不可以先後論，然舉理舉事，兩無所嫌，先後不其然乎？圖之論仁，參之以中正，類之以陰陽剛柔，則不得為專言之仁矣。偏指陽動之議，誠有所未宜。仁義中正，屬之以動靜，配之以元亨利貞，則脉絡分明，非支離穿鑿矣。分反其類之說，誠有所未當。不由師傳，獨得秘傳之旨，是也。誌文足以為此圖之明驗，种穆之學烏足以語此？立象盡意，示發精蘊之言，是也。《通書》所以闡此圖之蘊奧，先生之學將奚以加此？廣大詳備，太極之規模，方
translation_en:
…“The Master's essential insights are displayed through the diagram, and his profound understanding is unfolded through it.” What further doubt can there be? Yet critics say that he ought not to distinguish yin and yang by reference to “the continuation of goodness” and “the completion of nature.” They fail to understand that transformation is inexhaustible, whereas what each being receives as its endowment is determinate: the distinction between activity and stillness is perfectly clear. They also say that he ought not to distinguish the Way from concrete things by reference to the Supreme Ultimate and yin and yang. They fail to understand that the Supreme Ultimate has no form, whereas yin and yang possess material force: the distinction between what is above and what is below physical form is properly ordered.

Humaneness, righteousness, centrality, and correctness admittedly cannot simply be discussed in terms of substance and function. Yet the outgoing operation of sincerity and its return each have their respective affiliations; what harm is there in speaking of substance and function? Substance and function share a single source and admittedly cannot be discussed as preceding and following one another. Yet whether one speaks of principle or of concrete affairs, neither usage is objectionable. Is this not how precedence and succession should be understood?

When the diagram discusses humaneness, it associates it with centrality and correctness and classifies it in relation to yin and yang, firmness and yielding. It therefore cannot mean humaneness spoken of comprehensively. The objection that it refers narrowly to yang and activity is indeed somewhat inappropriate. When humaneness, righteousness, centrality, and correctness are assigned to activity and stillness and correlated with origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy, their connections are clear; this is no fragmented or strained interpretation. The claim that these divisions run counter to their proper categories is indeed somewhat mistaken.

It is correct that, without receiving instruction from a teacher, he independently grasped the purport of the secret transmission. The funerary inscription provides clear corroboration of this diagram. How could the learning of Chong and Mu suffice to explain it? It is correct to say that he established images to express his meaning fully and thereby displayed and unfolded his essential insights and profound understanding. The Book of Penetration (Tongshu) elucidates the depths and mysteries of this diagram. How could the Master's learning go beyond this? As for its breadth, detail, and completeness—the scope of the Supreme Ultimate—when comparing it with …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之伏羲先天圖誠有如終在範圍之說者
物理本一象數無二卒亦未甞不相爲表
裏也又豈學者可得而優劣之乎本末次
序太極之兼該比之張子論氣章誠有如
出入陰陽之論者圖說氣論各有發明終
亦未甞不相爲羽翼也又豈學者可得而
偏廢之乎嗚呼湯誥降衷烝民物則人知
性出於天而不知夫性之善大易善性七
篇仁義人知性無不善而不知夫善之由
===
周子因群聖之已言推其所未言而有此
太極圖之作正學者所當虛心一意反覆
沉潛究竟乎其所存所發之全體奧旨以
爲終身受用之地者也烏可執一偏之見
故爲是無稽之議而甘心於無星之秤尺
哉愚蓋讀朱子辯論而未之有得焉者願
進而教之
第四問
方以嘉
punctuated:
之伏羲先天圖，誠有如終在範圍之說者。物理本一，象數無二，卒亦未甞不相爲表裏也，又豈學者可得而優劣之乎？本末次序，太極之兼該，比之張子論氣章，誠有如出入陰陽之論者。圖說、氣論，各有發明，終亦未甞不相爲羽翼也，又豈學者可得而偏廢之乎？嗚呼！《湯誥》降衷，《烝民》物則，人知性出於天，而不知夫性之善；《大易》善性，七篇仁義，人知性無不善，而不知夫善之由。周子因群聖之已言，推其所未言，而有此太極圖之作，正學者所當虛心一意，反覆沉潛，究竟乎其所存所發之全體奧旨，以爲終身受用之地者也。烏可執一偏之見，故爲是無稽之議，而甘心於無星之秤尺哉？愚蓋讀朱子辯論，而未之有得焉者，願進而教之。

第四問

方以嘉
translation_en:
…with Fuxi’s Diagram of the Before-Heaven Order, there is indeed something to the claim that it ultimately falls within that diagram’s compass [?]. The principles of things are fundamentally one, and images and numbers are not two separate systems. In the end, they have always complemented one another as outer expression and inner substance. How, then, can scholars rank one above the other? In its comprehensive treatment of root and branch and their proper sequence, the Supreme Ultimate, compared with Master Zhang’s chapter discussing qi, does indeed accord with the argument concerning movement into and out of yin and yang [?]. The Explanation of the Diagram and the discussion of qi each illuminate something; in the end, they have always supported one another like a pair of wings. How, then, can scholars favor one and discard the other?

Alas! The Announcement of Tang speaks of Heaven’s bestowal of an inner moral norm, and the poem The Multitudes speaks of the standards inherent in things. People knew that human nature came from Heaven, but did not know that this nature was good. The great Book of Changes speaks of goodness and human nature, and the seven books of the Mencius speak of benevolence and righteousness. People knew that human nature was invariably good, but did not know why it was good. Building upon what the sages had already said, Master Zhou developed what they had left unsaid, and thus produced this Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. Scholars should therefore approach it with an open mind and undivided attention, pondering it repeatedly and deeply, and thoroughly investigating the complete substance and profound meaning of what it contains and expresses, so as to make it a foundation from which to draw benefit throughout their lives. How could they cling to a partial view, deliberately advance such groundless arguments, and willingly content themselves with scales and rulers lacking graduations? I, in my ignorance, have read Master Zhu’s arguments but have yet to gain an understanding of them. I venture to come forward and ask for instruction.

Fourth Policy Question

Fang Yijia

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導陳批士子多為問目所窘
此作條答明白不啻佩琳琅而鏘然其鳴寧不
欣愛
考試官學正周批於鄉邦道學之士歷
歷能道而詞足以達之當是策手
考試官教授張批道學源流悉數如見
其究心於此者乎
對道學之傳至閩中而益盛閩中之學至
朱子而極盛是皆關乎世道之治文運之
===
亨雖脩為之者有在於人而所以為之者
實出於天夫豈偶然而已者哉執事發策
而詢及吾閩道學之士愚雖末學嘗讀諸
家之書而知其人矣請歷陳之以復明問
可乎夫自孟子之沒而聖學失傳至宋文
運大開真儒輩出濂溪濬其源伊洛導其
流橫渠助其瀾而聖人之道始復明於世
厥功大矣然當是時閩士之遊於洛者則
有若龜山楊氏故程子之送其歸而有吾
punctuated:
同考試官訓導陳批：士子多為問目所窘，此作條答明白，不啻佩琳琅而鏘然其鳴，寧不欣愛？
考試官學正周批：於鄉邦道學之士，歷歷能道，而詞足以達之，當是策手。
考試官教授張批：道學源流悉數如見，其究心於此者乎？
對：道學之傳至閩中而益盛，閩中之學至朱子而極盛，是皆關乎世道之治、文運之亨。雖脩為之者有在於人，而所以為之者實出於天，夫豈偶然而已者哉？執事發策，而詢及吾閩道學之士，愚雖末學，嘗讀諸家之書而知其人矣。請歷陳之，以復明問，可乎？夫自孟子之沒，而聖學失傳，至宋文運大開，真儒輩出。濂溪濬其源，伊洛導其流，橫渠助其瀾，而聖人之道始復明於世，厥功大矣。然當是時，閩士之遊於洛者，則有若龜山楊氏，故程子之送其歸，而有「吾
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: Candidates are often stymied by the questions. This composition answers them point by point with clarity, like fine jade pendants ringing out as they are worn. How could one fail to delight in it?

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: He can give a distinct account of each of his native province’s scholars of the Learning of the Way, and his language adequately conveys his knowledge. Surely he is an accomplished writer of policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: He enumerates the origins and successive transmissions of the Learning of the Way as though they were before his eyes. Has he not devoted himself to studying this subject?

Response: The transmission of the Learning of the Way flourished still more upon reaching Fujian, and learning in Fujian reached its fullest flourishing with Master Zhu. All this bears upon good order in the world and the flourishing fortunes of literary culture. Although its cultivation and practice depend upon human beings, what makes them possible truly comes from Heaven. How could this have been merely accidental? You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question concerning the scholars of the Learning of the Way in our Fujian. Though I am but a humble novice in learning, I have read the writings of the various masters and have come to know these men. May I set them forth in succession to answer your discerning inquiry?

After the death of Mencius, the transmission of the sages’ learning was lost. With the Song, the fortunes of literary culture opened broadly, and true Confucian scholars appeared in succession. Lianxi dredged its source; the masters of Yi and Luo channeled its flow; Hengqu augmented its waves. Only then did the Way of the sages once again shine clearly in the world. Great indeed were their achievements! At that time, among the scholars of Fujian who traveled to Luo to study was Yang Guishan. Thus, when Master Cheng saw him off on his return home, he said, “My …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
道南矣之言蓋龜山之道卽程子之道也
龜山一傳而得羅仲素氏則潜思力行任
重詣極者也羅氏再傳而得李愿中氏則
氷壺秋月瑩徹無瑕者也程子之學蓋至
是焉益盛矣至於朱子又受之李氏則以
豪傑之才任聖賢之學易有本義詩有集
傳儀禮有解四書有註小學有書折衷群
言集其大成而其功之盛無以加矣故四
方學者擔簦負笈雲集其門而皆莫若閩
===
士之衆今試以其人言之爲朱子之壻而
註經解者有黃榦焉朱子呼爲老友而著
律呂新書者有蔡元定焉義理貫通洞見
條緒者則陳淳其人也端謹淳厚天質近
道者則李方子其人也潜心反覆數十年
而成書傳者非蔡沈乎篤志精思留朱子
之家而編中庸或問輯略者非李閎祖乎
他如楊復之附註家禮而及祭禮潘柄之
解易而及尚書則又皆朱門之高弟也夫
punctuated: 道南矣」之言，蓋龜山之道卽程子之道也。龜山一傳而得羅仲素氏，則潜思力行、任重詣極者也。羅氏再傳而得李愿中氏，則氷壺秋月、瑩徹無瑕者也。程子之學蓋至是焉益盛矣。至於朱子，又受之李氏，則以豪傑之才，任聖賢之學。《易》有《本義》，《詩》有《集傳》，《儀禮》有解，《四書》有註，《小學》有書，折衷群言，集其大成，而其功之盛無以加矣。故四方學者擔簦負笈，雲集其門，而皆莫若閩士之衆。今試以其人言之：爲朱子之壻而註經解者，有黃榦焉；朱子呼爲老友而著《律呂新書》者，有蔡元定焉；義理貫通、洞見條緒者，則陳淳其人也；端謹淳厚、天質近道者，則李方子其人也。潜心反覆數十年而成《書傳》者，非蔡沈乎？篤志精思，留朱子之家而編《中庸或問輯略》者，非李閎祖乎？他如楊復之附註《家禮》而及《祭禮》，潘柄之解《易》而及《尚書》，則又皆朱門之高弟也。夫
translation_en:
…“the Way has gone south!” For Guishan’s Way was precisely Master Cheng’s Way. In the first transmission from Guishan came Luo Zhongsu, who reflected deeply and acted resolutely, shouldering a weighty responsibility and attaining the highest reaches. In the second transmission, from Luo, came Li Yuanzhong, who was like an ice-filled vessel or the autumn moon, luminous and utterly without blemish. By this point, Master Cheng’s learning had indeed grown still more flourishing. Master Zhu, in turn, received it from Li. With the abilities of an outstanding man, he took upon himself the learning of the sages and worthies. For the Changes he produced the Original Meaning; for the Odes, the Collected Commentaries; for the Ceremonies and Rites, explanations; for the Four Books, annotations; and for elementary learning, a book. He weighed and reconciled the various teachings and brought them together into a grand synthesis. The magnitude of his achievement could not be surpassed.

Thus scholars from every quarter, carrying rain hats and book satchels, gathered at his gate like clouds; yet none matched the scholars of Fujian in number. Let us now speak of particular men. There was Huang Gan, Master Zhu’s son-in-law, who wrote annotations explaining the classics. There was Cai Yuanding, whom Master Zhu called his old friend, who wrote the New Book on Pitch Standards. Chen Chun thoroughly comprehended moral principles and clearly discerned their interconnected strands. Li Fangzi was upright, conscientious, sincere, and generous, with a natural disposition close to the Way. Was it not Cai Shen who devoted himself to repeated study for several decades and completed the Commentary on the Documents? Was it not Li Hongzu who, steadfast in purpose and meticulous in thought, stayed in Master Zhu’s household and compiled the Collected Essentials of Questions and Answers on the Mean? Others, such as Yang Fu, who added annotations to the Family Rituals and also treated the Sacrificial Rites, and Pan Bing, who explained the Changes and also the Book of Documents, were likewise all distinguished disciples of Master Zhu. Now, …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
龜山三傳而至朱子朱子再傳而及其門
人一脉之盛如此然自此之外又豈無其
人哉若游酢胡安國之與龜山則同聞道
伊洛者也胡寅之與胡宏則同從遊龜山
者也程子稱酢德器粹然學問日進而酢
所著有記其師之語謝良佐稱安國如大
冬嚴雪松柏獨茂而安國所著有春秋傳
則其人有可知矣胡寅之不附秦檜而著
讀史管見及論語詳說胡宏之優游南山
===
而著知言一書及皇王大紀則其人又可
知矣抑論之濂洛關閩諸儒迭出眞履實
踐著書立言上有以繼往聖下有以開來
學扶世植教之功固云同矣獨朱子於其
間功又有倍於諸儒者昔人之稱孔子有
曰先孔子而聖者非孔子無以明後孔子
而聖者非孔子無以法愚亦曰先朱子而
賢者非朱子無以明後朱子而賢者非朱
子無以法敢以斯言爲執事獻
punctuated:
龜山三傳而至朱子，朱子再傳而及其門人，一脉之盛如此。然自此之外，又豈無其人哉？若游酢、胡安國之與龜山，則同聞道伊洛者也；胡寅之與胡宏，則同從遊龜山者也。程子稱酢德器粹然，學問日進，而酢所著有記其師之語；謝良佐稱安國如大冬嚴雪，松柏獨茂，而安國所著有《春秋傳》，則其人有可知矣。胡寅之不附秦檜，而著《讀史管見》及《論語詳說》；胡宏之優游南山，而著《知言》一書及《皇王大紀》，則其人又可知矣。
抑論之，濂洛關閩諸儒迭出，眞履實踐，著書立言，上有以繼往聖，下有以開來學，扶世植教之功固云同矣。獨朱子於其間，功又有倍於諸儒者。昔人之稱孔子有曰：「先孔子而聖者，非孔子無以明；後孔子而聖者，非孔子無以法。」愚亦曰：「先朱子而賢者，非朱子無以明；後朱子而賢者，非朱子無以法。」敢以斯言爲執事獻。
translation_en:
… Through three transmissions from Guishan, the lineage reached Master Zhu; through two further transmissions from Master Zhu, it reached his disciples [?]. Such was the flourishing of this single lineage. Yet beyond these, were there not others worthy of mention? You Zuo and Hu Anguo, like Guishan, heard the Way taught in the Yi–Luo region; Hu Yin and Hu Hong both studied under Guishan. Master Cheng praised You Zuo for the purity of his moral character and capacity, and for his daily progress in learning; among You Zuo’s writings are records of his teacher’s sayings. Xie Liangzuo praised Hu Anguo as resembling the pine and cypress that alone flourish amid the harsh snows of deepest winter; among Hu Anguo’s writings is the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals. From these things, their character can be understood. Hu Yin refused to align himself with Qin Hui and wrote Limited Views on Reading History and Detailed Explanations of the Analects. Hu Hong dwelt at ease in Nanshan and wrote Understanding Words and the Grand Chronicle of Emperors and Kings. From these things, their character, too, can be understood.
To consider the matter further: the scholars of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min emerged in succession, earnestly putting their teachings into practice and setting forth their ideas in books. Looking back, they carried on the legacy of earlier sages; looking forward, they opened the way for later students. Their contributions to sustaining society and establishing moral teaching may certainly be called alike. Yet among them, Master Zhu’s achievement was greater still than those of the other scholars. Someone of former times praised Confucius, saying: “Without Confucius, the sages who preceded him could not have been made manifest; without Confucius, the sages who followed him would have had no model to follow.” I, in my humble opinion, would likewise say: “Without Master Zhu, the worthies who preceded him could not have been made manifest; without Master Zhu, the worthies who followed him would have had no model to follow.” I venture to submit these words to you, honored examiner.

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第五問
陳邦彥
同考試官訓導胡批〔此策淺近人多忽而〕
〔不考是篇條答無遺非掛一漏萬者可比蓋得〕
〔於父兄師友之教有素矣〕
考試官學正周批〔知童蒙始學之方必〕
〔有能正法者〕
考試官教授張批〔聲音之辨塲中答者〕
〔不甚詳惟此悉能考之是用錄出〕
===
讀山下出泉之象則知蒙不可以不養讀
蒙養弗端之戒則知養不可以不正蓋不
養失之初長則扞格不勝而教無所施不
正流於妄長則益習浮靡而教為徒然故
父兄師友之於子弟烏可失其養而昧所
學之正哉請撫拾平日之授受以復其萬
一粵昔字母未撰未聞聲音有辨孰知所
趨逮沈約常撰其字母以第一第二為平
為上以第三第四為去為入是之謂四聲
punctuated:
第五問
陳邦彥
同考試官訓導胡批〔此策淺近，人多忽而〕〔不考。是篇條答無遺，非掛一漏萬者可比，蓋得〕〔於父兄師友之教有素矣。〕
考試官學正周批〔知童蒙始學之方，必〕〔有能正法者。〕
考試官教授張批〔聲音之辨，塲中答者〕〔不甚詳，惟此悉能考之，是用錄出。〕
讀「山下出泉」之象，則知蒙不可以不養；讀「蒙養弗端」之戒，則知養不可以不正。蓋不養，失之初，長則扞格不勝，而教無所施；不正，流於妄，長則益習浮靡，而教為徒然。故父兄師友之於子弟，烏可失其養而昧所學之正哉？請撫拾平日之授受，以復其萬一。粵昔字母未撰，未聞聲音有辨，孰知所趨？逮沈約常撰其字母，以第一、第二為平、為上，以第三、第四為去、為入，是之謂四聲。
translation_en:
Fifth Policy Question
Chen Bangyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor: “This policy question concerns elementary matters that many people overlook and fail to investigate. This essay answers each point without omission; it cannot be compared with answers that mention one thing and omit ten thousand. Clearly, its author has long benefited from instruction by fathers and elder brothers, teachers and friends.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “He understands how young beginners should start learning; surely someone capable has guided him in the correct methods.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “On distinctions among speech sounds, the candidates in the examination hall have not answered in much detail. This essay alone examines them all, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”

Reading the image, “A spring issues from beneath a mountain,” we understand that the unformed young must be nurtured. Reading the admonition against “failing to nurture the young correctly,” we understand that their nurture must be proper. Without nurture, they go astray at the outset; when grown, their resistance becomes insurmountable, and instruction has no purchase. Without proper guidance, they drift into error; when grown, they become increasingly accustomed to frivolity and extravagance, and instruction proves futile. How, then, can fathers and elder brothers, teachers and friends neglect the nurture of the younger generation and remain ignorant of what is correct in their learning? Allow me to gather what I have ordinarily received through instruction and offer a small part of it in reply.

In ancient times, before phonetic letters had been compiled, distinctions among speech sounds were unheard of: who knew which course to follow? When Shen Yue compiled his phonetic letters [?], he designated the first and second as the level and rising tones, and the third and fourth as the departing and entering tones. These are called the four tones.

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫初學之方惟此爲要調不宜所先乎初
聲轉聲爲平爲仄無形有跡爲虛爲實死
則體本乎靜生則用發乎動是之謂六體
夫平仄既辨字義須識明不居其次乎字
譜未作未聞切韻有律孰知所向及夫唐
人作其字譜以縮却點齒居中之聲屬乎
角徵宮以口張撮聚之聲屬乎商與羽哀
而安厲而舉有得平上之義然也清而遠
直而促有合去入之義爾也東方北方其
===
人之言語常重濁而不輕清蓋以出自喉
與唇而混於風俗之相染也西南中央其
人之言語常輕清而不重濁蓋以出自舌
齒牙而兼乎風俗之相習也然清者其音
屬徵屬角屬羽濁者其音屬宮屬商調聲
之法舉左手拇指輪巡以食指根主平其
頭主上而連續用之以無名指根主入其
頭主去而次序輪之而中指不與者謂非
象一字之有四角乎至若撮唇之訣有如
punctuated: 夫初學之方，惟此爲要，調不宜所先乎？初聲轉聲，爲平爲仄；無形有跡，爲虛爲實；死則體本乎靜，生則用發乎動。是之謂六體。夫平仄既辨，字義須識，明不居其次乎？字譜未作，未聞切韻有律，孰知所向？及夫唐人作其字譜，以縮却、點齒、居中之聲屬乎角、徵、宮，以口張、撮聚之聲屬乎商與羽。哀而安，厲而舉，有得平上之義然也；清而遠，直而促，有合去入之義爾也。東方北方，其人之言語常重濁而不輕清，蓋以出自喉與唇，而混於風俗之相染也。西南中央，其人之言語常輕清而不重濁，蓋以出自舌齒牙，而兼乎風俗之相習也。然清者，其音屬徵、屬角、屬羽；濁者，其音屬宮、屬商。調聲之法，舉左手拇指輪巡，以食指根主平，其頭主上，而連續用之；以無名指根主入，其頭主去，而次序輪之。而中指不與者，謂非象一字之有四角乎？至若撮唇之訣，有如
translation_en:
As for the method of beginning study, this alone is essential: ought the regulation of tones not to come first [?]? Initial and altered sounds constitute the level and oblique categories; what has no form and what has discernible traces constitute the empty and substantial categories; in the dead category, the essential form is grounded in stillness, while in the living category, its function issues in movement. These are called the six forms. Once level and oblique tones have been distinguished, the meanings of characters must be understood: does understanding not come next?

Before charts of characters were made, no rules for indicating rhymes by the fanqie method were known; who could know which way to proceed? When people of the Tang compiled their charts of characters, they assigned sounds produced by drawing back, touching the teeth, and occupying the middle to the musical notes jue, zhi, and gong, and sounds produced by opening the mouth and drawing it together to shang and yu. Mournful and settled, forceful and raised: these capture the meanings of the level and rising tones. Clear and far-reaching, straight and abrupt: these accord with the meanings of the departing and entering tones.

In the east and north, people's speech is generally heavy and turbid rather than light and clear. This is because it issues from the throat and lips and is mingled through the mutual influence of local customs. In the west, south, and central regions, people's speech is generally light and clear rather than heavy and turbid. This is because it issues from the tongue, front teeth, and molars, combined with habits acquired through local customs. Clear sounds belong to zhi, jue, and yu; turbid sounds belong to gong and shang.

The method of regulating tones is to raise the left thumb and move it around in turn. The base of the index finger represents the level tone and its tip the rising tone; use these consecutively. The base of the ring finger represents the entering tone and its tip the departing tone; cycle through these in order. As for excluding the middle finger, could this not be said to imitate the four corners of a single character? As for the formula for rounding the lips, examples include…

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
呼虎烏塢汚之類是已齊齒之訣有如時
之實始成之類是已曰勾狗鷗鴉此則引
喉之法也曰臻櫛詵生此則平牙之法也
若合口則品於甘鹹檻甲訣可知矣若捲
舌則品於伊幽乙英訣可想矣唇上觀諸
碧班邠豹之字正齒觀諸止征眞志之字
縱唇之訣非無稽也必推之於鳩九休求
口開之訣非妄議也必推之於何可歌羹
查挐宅帳聲固別矣蓋由在人之氣隨所
===
送而出也蒿豪好赫聲亦殊矣蓋因在人
之鼻隨所動而發也曰囂妖曰嬌矯轎則
上鄂之訣又在是矣他如聲者心之動也
聲出而雙如劉禹錫云出谷嬌鶯新晛睆
營巢乳燕舊呢喃觀於此詩則雙聲之說
奚待辨諸頰舌而後知哉韻者聲之轉也
韻咏而疊如杜甫云卑枝低結子接葉暗
巢鶯驗於此詩則疊韻之說奚勞析諸口
語而後明哉是學也雖若細故而他無所
punctuated:
呼、虎、烏、塢、汚之類是已。齊齒之訣，有如時、之、實、始、成之類是已。曰勾、狗、鷗、鴉，此則引喉之法也；曰臻、櫛、詵、生，此則平牙之法也。若合口，則品於甘、鹹、檻、甲，訣可知矣；若捲舌，則品於伊、幽、乙、英，訣可想矣。唇上觀諸碧、班、邠、豹之字，正齒觀諸止、征、眞、志之字。縱唇之訣，非無稽也，必推之於鳩、九、休、求；口開之訣，非妄議也，必推之於何、可、歌、羹。查、挐、宅、帳，聲固別矣，蓋由在人之氣隨所送而出也。蒿、豪、好、赫，聲亦殊矣，蓋因在人之鼻隨所動而發也。曰囂、妖，曰嬌、矯、轎，則上鄂之訣又在是矣。
他如聲者，心之動也，聲出而雙。如劉禹錫云：「出谷嬌鶯新晛睆，營巢乳燕舊呢喃。」觀於此詩，則雙聲之說，奚待辨諸頰舌而後知哉？韻者，聲之轉也，韻咏而疊。如杜甫云：「卑枝低結子，接葉暗巢鶯。」驗於此詩，則疊韻之說，奚勞析諸口語而後明哉？是學也，雖若細故，而他無所
translation_en:
…examples such as 呼, 虎, 烏, 塢, and 汚 illustrate it. The technique of aligning the teeth is illustrated by examples such as 時, 之, 實, 始, and 成. Pronouncing 勾, 狗, 鷗, and 鴉 illustrates the method of drawing the sound through the throat; pronouncing 臻, 櫛, 詵, and 生 illustrates the method of keeping the back teeth level. For closing the mouth, examine the sounds 甘, 鹹, 檻, and 甲, and the technique can be understood. For curling the tongue, examine 伊, 幽, 乙, and 英, and the technique can be conceived. For sounds on the lips, observe the characters 碧, 班, 邠, and 豹; for aligning the front teeth, observe 止, 征, 眞, and 志. The technique of relaxing the lips is not without foundation: it must be investigated through 鳩, 九, 休, and 求. The technique of opening the mouth is not idle speculation: it must be investigated through 何, 可, 歌, and 羹. 查, 挐, 宅, and 帳 certainly differ in sound; this results from a person's breath emerging according to how it is directed. 蒿, 豪, 好, and 赫 also differ in sound; this results from sounds issuing through a person's nose according to its movement. Pronounce 囂 and 妖, and then 嬌, 矯, and 轎: here, too, lies the technique involving the upper palate [?].
Furthermore, sound is the stirring of the heart; as sounds emerge, their initials may be paired. As Liu Yuxi says: “Emerging from the valley, lovely orioles newly shine bright-eyed [?]; building their nests, young swallows twitter as of old.” Looking at this poem, why must one distinguish the workings of cheeks and tongue before understanding paired initials? Rhyme is the turning of sound; in chanting, rhymes may recur. As Du Fu says: “Low branches bear fruit close to the ground; amid overlapping leaves, orioles nest unseen.” Examining this poem, why take the trouble to analyze spoken utterances before understanding repeated rhymes? Although this learning may seem a minor matter, with no connection to anything else …

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
與殊不知聲律旣正則放心可收由此言
可以通乎道聲可以宣乎言小可以造乎
大近可以及乎遠洒掃應對之節修齊治
平之理皆可因言而得之矣聖賢之閫雖
難入也可由此而入君子之奧雖難造也
可由此而造行由是順志由是應剛由是
中果何者而不造端於此哉若夫詩賦詞
章之句黼黻皇猷之文特其支流而已耳
噫蒙學雖小所關甚大其弟子於童稚之
===
年爲父兄師友者當何如哉亦曰養之以
正而已謹對
punctuated:
與。殊不知，聲律旣正，則放心可收。由此，言可以通乎道，聲可以宣乎言，小可以造乎大，近可以及乎遠。洒掃應對之節，修齊治平之理，皆可因言而得之矣。聖賢之閫雖難入也，可由此而入；君子之奧雖難造也，可由此而造。行由是順，志由是應，剛由是中，果何者而不造端於此哉？若夫詩賦詞章之句，黼黻皇猷之文，特其支流而已耳。
噫！蒙學雖小，所關甚大。其弟子於童稚之年，爲父兄師友者當何如哉？亦曰養之以正而已。謹對。
translation_en:
…have no bearing on other matters. Yet this overlooks the fact that, once the rules of sounds are correctly observed, the wayward mind can be brought back under control. Through this, words can communicate the Way, and sounds can give expression to words; the small can lead to the great, and the near can reach the distant. The proprieties of sprinkling and sweeping, answering and responding, and the principles of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world can all be apprehended through words. Though the threshold of the sages and worthies is difficult to enter, one can enter by this means; though the inner sanctuary of the gentleman is difficult to reach, one can reach it by this means. Conduct thereby becomes correct, purpose becomes responsive, and firmness attains due measure. What, indeed, does not have its beginnings here? As for lines of poetry, rhapsodies, and literary compositions, and writings that embellish imperial policies, these are merely its subsidiary branches.
Ah! Elementary learning may seem a small matter, but its implications are very great. While sons and younger brothers are still children, what should those who are their fathers, elder brothers, teachers, and friends do? The answer is simply to nurture them through what is correct. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 弘治十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
弘治戊午秋士當大比先是
閩省藩臬重臣以事謀于巡
按監察御史張敏走聘淵等
以司文柄及期合八郡之士
而三試之遵
定制取九十名刻文之雋者為
===
錄以
獻淵宜序諸末竊惟三代無文
人六經無文法非無文人也
不以文論人非無文法也不
以文為法文以載道道得於
心而形於言言之成章則曰
文耳古謂仁義之人其言藹
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

弘治戊午秋，士當大比。先是，閩省藩臬重臣以事謀于巡按監察御史張敏，走聘淵等以司文柄。及期，合八郡之士而三試之，遵定制取九十名，刻文之雋者為錄以獻。淵宜序諸末。竊惟三代無文人，六經無文法。非無文人也，不以文論人；非無文法也，不以文為法。文以載道，道得於心而形於言，言之成章則曰文耳。古謂仁義之人，其言藹
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the wuwu year of the Hongzhi reign [1498], scholars were due to sit the triennial examination. Before this, the senior officials of Fujian’s Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission consulted the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Zhang Min, about the matter and dispatched an invitation to me, Yuan, and others to take charge of literary assessment. At the appointed time, candidates from the eight prefectures were assembled and examined in three sessions. In accordance with established regulations, ninety were selected, and the outstanding essays were carved for printing as a record to be presented to the throne. It falls to me, Yuan, to append a postface.

I venture to reflect that the Three Dynasties had no literary specialists, and the Six Classics had no rules of composition.
